I wrote both trust files and the gate check passed on the first run. **Verdict:** The About page made Nimbus Notes feel like a real company, but neither visitor trusted it with money or data: no price exists, and the cookie bar's "no tracking" claim is contradicted by the privacy page and by a tracker firing on landing. **Score:** 3/10. Both visitors believed a real company is behind the site, then one refused to pay without a price and the other left over how her data is handled. **Count by severity (8 findings):** | Severity | Count | Findings | |---|---|---| | P0 | 1 | The cookie bar says "no tracking cookies", but a third-party analytics script loads and posts a user ID on landing (both personas) | | P1 | 3 | • The privacy page names no partners and contradicts the cookie bar, so the sceptic left
• No plan shows a price, so the evaluator gave up
• The demo form requires a phone number, and the evaluator backed out | | P2 | 3 | • The evaluator was left unsure about their data by the privacy page
• All three testimonials are anonymous
• "See it in action" does nothing | | P3 | 1 | The answer to where data is stored ("Frankfurt") is on the About page, not the Privacy page | **Severity flip:** the unnamed privacy partners are P1 for the sceptic, because that is why she left. For the evaluator they are P2, because price was their reason to leave. The sceptic never looked for a price, so a flip on pricing could not be observed. **Dropped for want of evidence:** - The demo-form screenshot (`03-demo-form.png`) is blank, so that finding rests only on the session log. - Nobody reacted to the hero claim "nothing you write is ever lost or exposed". - Nobody remarked that the privacy page sends questions to "Use the demo form." Both personas are generic (inferred, not researched), and the report says so in both files. The gate also noted that the run itself hasn't been closed yet (`close_run.py`).
